When she had bought the chest, carried it, and set off with it, the carpenter went to the slaughterers to inform them about the matter of the mother of Moses. When he began to speak, God seized his tongue, and he could not speak. He began to gesture with his hand, and the officials did not understand what he meant. When his matter perplexed them, their chief said: "Strike him!" So they struck him and drove him out. When the carpenter reached his place, God restored his tongue to him, and he spoke. He went again, intending the officials, to inform them, but God seized his tongue and his sight, so he could not speak and could see nothing. They struck him and drove him out, and he fell into a valley where he wandered in bewilderment. God made a condition for him: if He restored his tongue and sight, he would not inform on him and would be with him to protect him wherever he was. God knew the truthfulness in him, so He restored his tongue and sight to him, and he fell down prostrate before God. He said: "O Lord, guide me to this righteous servant." Pharaoh's daughter came with her maidservants until she sat on the bank of the Nile with her maidservants, playing with them and sprinkling water on their faces. Suddenly the Nile brought the chest, tossed by the waves. Pharaoh said: "Indeed, this is something in the sea that has become entangled with the tree. Bring it to me!" They rushed to it with boats from every side until they placed it before him. They tried to open the lid but could not, and they tried to break it but could not. Then Asiya drew near and saw in the inside of the chest a light which no one else saw. She worked at it and opened the lid, and there was a small child in his cradle, and a light between his eyes, and God had placed his provision in his thumb, which he sucked for milk. God cast love for Moses into Asiya's heart, and Pharaoh also loved him and was affectionate toward him. Pharaoh's daughter came up, and when they took the child out of the chest, she went to the saliva that had been flowing from his mouth, smeared it on her leprosy, and was healed. She kissed him and pressed him to her chest. The deviants among Pharaoh's people said: "O king, we think that this is the newborn you are warning against from the Children of Israel. He was thrown into the sea out of fear of you, so kill him!" Pharaoh resolved to kill him. Asiya said: "The delight of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son," for she could not bear children. So she asked Pharaoh to give her Moses as a gift, and he gave him to her. Pharaoh said: "As for me, I have no need of him."

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If Pharaoh had said on that day, 'He is the delight of the eye for me as he is for you,' God would have guided him as He guided her." **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 28, verses 8–9:**

This lam is called lam al-'aqibah (the lam of consequence) and lam al-sayrurah (the lam of outcome), because they did not pick him up in order that he would become for them an enemy and a grief. Rather, the outcome of their affair turned out to be that. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ḥuznan" with a damma on the ḥa and a sukun on the zay. The others read it with a fatha on the ḥa and the zay. Both are dialectal forms. ﴿Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers were ever sinners﴾: ʿāṣīn (disobedient), āthimīn (sinful).

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said: "A comfort of the eye for me and for you."﴾ Wahb said: When the chest was placed before Pharaoh, they opened it and found Moses in it. Pharaoh had taken as a wife a woman from the Children of Israel called Asiyah bint Muzahim. She was among the best of women, one of the daughters of the prophets, and a mother to the needy: she showed them mercy, gave them charity, and provided for them. She said to Pharaoh while she was sitting beside him: "This child is older than a year-old infant. You only ordered that the boys be slaughtered in this year. So leave him to be a comfort of the eye for me and for you." ﴿Do not kill him.﴾ It is also narrated that she said to him: "He has come to us from another land, not from the Children of Israel." ﴿Perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son,﴾ and they did not perceive [that] their destruction would be at his hands. So Pharaoh spared him, and Allah cast His love upon him. He said to his wife: "Perhaps he will benefit you, but as for me, I do not desire his benefit." Wahb said: Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "If the enemy of Allah had said about Moses what Asiyah said, 'Perhaps he will benefit us,' Allah would have benefited him. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 15:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And he entered the city﴾, meaning Musa entered the city. Al-Suddi said: It was the city of "Manf" (Memphis) in the land of Egypt. Muqatil said: It was the village of "Habin," two farsakhs from Egypt. It was also said: It was the city of "Ayn al-Shams" [[In "A": ʿAyn Shams.]]. ﴿At a time of heedlessness of its people﴾, at the time of the midday rest (al-qa'ilah), when people were occupied with their midday rest. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: He entered it between maghrib and 'isha'.

They differed about the reason why he entered the city at this time. Al-Suddi said: That is because Musa, peace be upon him, was called the son of Pharaoh. He would ride Pharaoh's mounts and wear clothing like his. One day Pharaoh rode out, and Musa was not with him. When Musa came, he was told: Pharaoh has ridden out. So he rode after him and was overtaken by the midday rest in the land of Manf. He entered it at midday, and there was no one in its outskirts. This is the meaning of His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿And he entered the city at a time of heedlessness of its people﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: Musa had a following (shi'ah) among the Children of Israel who listened to him and followed him. When he came to know the truth that he was upon, he saw the separation of Pharaoh and his people, and he opposed them in their religion, until this was mentioned about him and they feared him and he feared them. So he would not enter a town except in fear and in a state of being hidden. One day he entered it at a time of heedlessness of its people.

Ibn Zayd said: When Musa struck Pharaoh with the staff in his childhood, Pharaoh wanted to kill him. His wife said: He is a child. So Pharaoh left off killing him and ordered that he be removed from his city. He did not enter upon them again until he had grown and reached his full strength (ashuddah). So he entered the city at a time of heedlessness of its people, meaning: from the mention of Musa; that is, after they had forgotten his news and his affair because their time with him had become distant.

It is related from Ali, regarding His words "at a time of heedlessness," that it was a festival day for them, when they were occupied with their amusement and play.

﴿And he found in it two men fighting﴾, quarrelling and contending, ﴿one of them from his own party (shi'atihi)﴾, from the Children of Israel, ﴿and the other from his enemy﴾, from the Copts (al-Qibt). It was said: The one from his party was al-Samiri, and the one from his enemy was a Copt; it was said his name was Falsthun, the cook of Pharaoh. It was also said: "This is from his party, and this is from his enemy" means: this one is a believer and this one is an unbeliever. The Copt would conscript the Israelite to carry firewood to the kitchen.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas: When Musa reached his full strength, none of the family of Pharaoh could reach any of the Children of Israel with oppression, until they were restrained with complete restraint. The Children of Israel had grown mighty through Musa's position, because they knew that he was one of them. So Musa found two men fighting, one of them from the Children of Israel and the other from the family of Pharaoh. ﴿So the one from his party sought his help against the one from his enemy﴾. The Israelite sought his aid against the Pharaonic man. Al-istighatha is seeking aid (talab al-ghawth). So Musa became angry and his anger intensified, because the man had attacked him while knowing Musa's standing among the Children of Israel and his protection of them. People did not know anything except that he was related to them through nursing from Musa's mother. So he said to the Pharaonic man: Let him go. He said: I only seized him to carry firewood to your father's kitchen. So he disputed with him, and the Pharaonic man said: [62a] ﴿Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday?﴾ Musa had been given stature in creation and strength in power and force.

﴿So Musa struck him﴾. Ibn Mas'ud read: "fa-lakazahu Musa" (فَلَكَزَهُ مُوسَى), and the meaning of both is one, namely striking with the joined palm. It was said: al-wakz (الْوَكْز) is striking on the chest, and al-lakz (اللَّكْز) is on the back. Al-Farra' said: The meaning of both is one, namely pushing. Abu Ubayda said: al-wakz is pushing with the fingertips. In some tafsir works: Musa folded (his fingers) into a fist, and struck him in the chest. ﴿So he dispatched him﴾, meaning he killed him and finished with his affair. Everything you finish, you have qadaytahu and qadayta 'alayhi. So Musa, peace be upon him, regretted it, and his intention had not been killing. So he buried him in the sand. ﴿He said: This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is an enemy, a misleader, clearly misleading﴾, meaning: manifestly in error.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verses 16–17:

﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me,"﴾ by killing the Copt without having been commanded to, ﴿so He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾

﴿He said, "My Lord, for that with which You have blessed me"﴾ with forgiveness, ﴿I will never be a supporter﴾ helper ﴿of the criminals.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: "of the disbelievers." This indicates that the Israelite whom Musa helped was a disbeliever, and this is the view of Muqatil. Qatadah said: "I will never again help anyone in sin after this." Ibn Abbas said: "He did not make an exception (by saying 'if Allah wills'), so he was tested with it on the following day."

Ibn 'Abbas said: Pharaoh was approached and told, "The Children of Israel have killed a man from among us, so take our right from them." He said, "Find for me his killer and a witness against him, for it is not right to judge without evidence." Ibn 'Abbas said: when Pharaoh sent the executioners to kill Moses, they took the main road.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 28, verses 21–23:**

﴿So he left from there﴾, Musa, ﴿fearful and watching (for pursuit)﴾, i.e., awaiting the pursuers. ﴿He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people,"﴾ meaning the disbelievers. In the story: Pharaoh sent (men) in pursuit of him when he was informed of his flight, and said, "Ride along the high paths of the road, for he does not know how the road goes."

﴿And when he headed toward Madyan (Midian)﴾, i.e., he set out in its direction, proceeding toward it. It is said: "His house is opposite (tilqa') the house of so-and-so," when it faces it. Its root is from liqa' (meeting). Al-Zajjaj said: it means he took the road that lay opposite Madyan. Madyan is Madyan ibn Ibrahim, and the town was named after him. Musa had left in fear, without a mount, without sandals, and without provisions. Madyan was eight days' journey from Egypt. ﴿He said, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way,"﴾ i.e., the straight road to Madyan. He said this because he had not known the way to it before. When he prayed, an angel came to him holding a staff (anaza) and led him to Madyan. The exegetes said: Musa left Egypt with no food except the leaves of trees and herbs, until the greenness of them could be seen in his belly, and he did not reach Madyan until the soles of his feet had worn away. Ibn Abbas said: this was the first trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that Musa (peace be upon him) faced.

﴿And when he came to the water of Madyan﴾, which is a well from which they used to water their livestock, ﴿he found there a community﴾, a group ﴿of people watering (their flocks)﴾, ﴿and he found, apart from them,﴾ meaning besides the group, ﴿two women holding back (tadhuddan)﴾, meaning they were holding back and keeping their sheep away from the water until the people had finished and the well was clear for them. Al-Hasan said: they were restraining the sheep from mixing with the people's sheep. Qatadah said: they were restraining the people from their sheep. It was also said: they were preventing their sheep from straying and running off. The first opinion is the most correct, because of what follows, namely his saying: ﴿He said﴾, meaning Musa to the two women, ﴿"What is your business?"﴾, i.e., what is your situation that you do not water your livestock with the people? ﴿They said, "We cannot water (our flocks) until the shepherds take their flocks away (yusdir al-ri'a'),"﴾ Abu Ja'far, Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir recited yasdura with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the dal, meaning intransitive: until the shepherds return from the water. The others recited yusdira with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the dal, meaning transitive: until they themselves drive their livestock away from the water. Al-Ri'a' is the plural of ra'in, like tajir and tujjar. The meaning of the verse: "We do not water our livestock until the shepherds have finished, because we are two women who cannot water (them) and cannot compete with the men. When they have left, we water our livestock with what remains of their flocks in the trough."

﴿And our father is a very old man﴾, who cannot water his livestock, so we had to undertake the watering of the sheep ourselves. They differed about the name of their father. Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi and al-Hasan said: he was Shu'ayb, the Prophet (peace be upon him). Wahb ibn Munabbih and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: he was Yathrun, the nephew of Shu'ayb, and Shu'ayb had died before that, after losing his sight, and was buried between the Maqam and Zamzam.[^1] It was also said: he was a man who had believed in Shu'ayb.[^2]

They said: when Musa heard their words, he had mercy on them and uprooted a boulder from the mouth of another well nearby, which only a group of people could lift.

Ibn Ishaq said: Musa pushed the people aside and kept them away from the mouth of the well, and watered the women's sheep. It is also narrated that when the people returned with their flocks, they had covered the mouth of the well with a stone that only ten men could lift, and Musa came and lifted the stone alone, and watered the women's sheep. It is also said that he drew one bucket and prayed for blessing upon it, and all the sheep drank from it.[^3] This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So he watered (their flocks) for them, then withdrew into the shade﴾.

[^1]: Ibn Kathir said: this is found in the books of the Children of Israel.

[^2]: al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him (20/62), said: "This is among the matters whose knowledge can only be attained by a reliable report, and there is no report about it that establishes proof. So no opinion is closer to the truth than what Allah, Exalted is His praise, has said..." After mentioning the earlier opinions, Ibn Kathir said (3/385–386): "Others said: Shu'ayb lived a long time before the time of Musa (peace be upon him), because he said to his people: ﴿and the people of Lut are not far from you﴾ [11:89], and the destruction of the people of Lut occurred in the time of Khalil (Ibrahim, peace be upon him), by the explicit text of the Qur'an. It is known that between Khalil and Musa (peace be upon them both) there was a long period exceeding four hundred years, as mentioned by more than one scholar. As for what is said, that Shu'ayb lived a very long time, it is—and Allah knows best—a way of avoiding this difficulty. Then, among what strengthens the view that he was not Shu'ayb: if he were, it would have been likely that his name would be stated explicitly in the Qur'an here. As for what came in some hadiths of an explicit mention of him in the story of Musa, its chain of narration is not sound."

Therefore Ustadh Sayyid Qutb said in "Fi Zilal al-Qur'an" (5/2687), note (1), the Dar al-Shuruq edition: "...And I now incline to the view that he is not Shu'ayb, but another old man of Madyan. What leads to this preference is that this man is a very old man. Shu'ayb witnessed the destruction of his people, who had denied him, and none remained with him except the believers. So if he had been Shu'ayb the Prophet, among the rest of his believing people, they would not have watered (their flocks) before the two daughters of their prophet, who was an old man. This is not the behaviour of believing people, nor their treatment of their prophet and his daughters from the very first generation! In addition to this: the Qur'an mentions nothing about his teaching Musa, his son-in-law; and if it were Shu'ayb the Prophet, we would have heard the voice of prophethood in something of this with Musa, given that he lived with him for ten years."

[^3]: Al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah in "al-Musannaf", 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, narrated a report on this from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ibn Kathir related it in summary. See: al-Musannaf 11/530–531; al-Mustadrak 2/407; al-Tabari 20/64; al-Durr al-Manthur 6/405; Ibn Kathir 3/385. None of the reports cited by the exegetes contains a hadith traced to the Prophet ﷺ concerning the evidences of Musa's strength (peace be upon him), such as lifting the stone that covers the well, which, they said, only twenty or forty or more or fewer could lift. Rather, the shepherds were watering, and Musa pushed them aside and watered for the two women, or watered for them together with the shepherds.

There is no need for what many exegetes narrated about the evidences of his trustworthiness from his saying to the girl: "Walk behind me and guide me to the road," lest the wind reveal her... All of this is unnecessary artifice, and a removal of a suspicion that does not exist. Musa (peace be upon him) was chaste in his gaze and clean in his disposition, and so was she. When he prayed, an angel came to him holding a staff (anaza) and led him to Madyan. The exegetes said: Musa left Egypt with no food except the leaves of trees and herbs, until the greenness of them could be seen in his belly, and he did not reach Madyan until the soles of his feet had worn away. Ibn Abbas said: this was the first trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that Musa (peace be upon him) faced.

﴿And when he came to the water of Madyan﴾, which is a well from which they used to water their livestock, ﴿he found there a community﴾, a group ﴿of people watering (their flocks)﴾, ﴿and he found, apart from them,﴾ meaning besides the group, ﴿two women holding back (tadhuddan)﴾, meaning they were holding back and keeping their sheep away from the water until the people had finished and the well was clear for them. It was also said: they were preventing their sheep from straying and running off. [^1]: Ibn Kathir said: this is found in the books of the Children of Israel.

[^2]: al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him (20/62), said: "This is among the matters whose knowledge can only be attained by a reliable report, and there is no report about it that establishes proof. Al-hijaj (sing. hijjah) means years. ﴿"And if you complete ten, it is from you"﴾ — that is: if you complete ten years, that is a favour and a voluntary act from you, not obligatory upon you. ﴿"And I do not wish to burden you"﴾ — that is: I do not wish to oblige you to complete the ten, unless you volunteer. ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous."﴾ Umar said: that is, in good companionship and fulfilling what you have said.

Moses said: "That is between me and you." That is, this condition is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms you have imposed on me, I will fulfill it, and whichever you have stipulated concerning the marriage of one of them to me, it is up to me (in one manuscript: "علي" [upon me]). The matter is settled between us. Then the speech is complete. He then said: ﴿Whichever of the two terms I fulfill﴾. That is, whichever of the two terms: "ما" is extra (ṣilah), and "qaḍaytu" means I completed and finished it, whether the eight or the ten years. ﴿Then there shall be no injustice against me﴾, meaning there shall be no wrong done to me by my being pressed to serve beyond them. ﴿And God is Witness over what we say﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said: "a Witness over what is between me and you." It was also said: "a Guardian."

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahim informed us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman informed us, Marwan ibn Shuja' informed us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: A Jew from the people of al-Hirah asked me: "Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill?" I said: "I do not know until I go to the best of the Arabs (in al-Bukhari: the scholar [ḥibr] of the Arabs) and ask him." So I came and asked Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He fulfilled the more complete and the better of them. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said he would do something, he did it." (Related by al-Bukhari in al-Shahadat, chapter "Whoever orders the fulfilment of a promise": 5/289-290. The phrase "the Messenger of God (ﷺ)" here refers to whoever is characterised by this, and does not intend a specific person.)

It is also related from Abu Dharr, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "If you are asked, 'Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill?', say: 'The better and more righteous of them.' And if you are asked, 'Which of the two women did he marry?', say: 'The younger of them, the one who came and said, "O my father, hire him."' He married the younger of them and fulfilled the more complete of the two terms." (Related by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat: 2/19, and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 2/128.

Al-Haythami said (8/203): "Al-Tabarani related it in al-Saghir and al-Awsat, and al-Bazzar in summary; in the isnad of al-Tabarani is Uwayd ibn Abi Imran al-Jawni, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared weak, while Ibn Hibban judged him trustworthy, and the rest of al-Tabarani's narrators are trustworthy." See also 7/88. Ibn Kathir (3/387) cited it from the narration of al-Bazzar, who said: "We do not know it to be related from Abu Dharr except by this isnad," and in its isnad is "Uwayd..." Ibn Abi Hatim related it from a different route, containing an odd addition.)

Wahb said: "He married him to the elder (al-Kubra)." (No authentic report from the Prophet (ﷺ) has come concerning which of them he married, the younger or the elder. It suffices us what is in the Book of God, the Exalted, that he wished to marry him to one of his two daughters. Had knowing her name been of benefit, God would have named her in His Book. And God knows best.)

It is also related traced to Shaddad ibn Aws, to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Shu'ayb wept [out of love for God, Mighty and Majestic] until he went blind, and God restored his sight; then he wept until he went blind, and God restored his sight; then he wept until he went blind, and God restored his sight. God said: 'What is this weeping? Is it longing for Paradise or fear of the Fire?' He said: 'No, my Lord, but longing for Your meeting.' So God revealed to him: 'If it is so, then congratulations to you for meeting Me, O Shu'ayb. For this I made Moses, My interlocutor, your servant.'" ([The bracketed words are absent from both manuscripts; I have restored them from Tarikh Baghdad, where al-Khatib related it with his isnad from Shaddad ibn Aws, traced to the Prophet.] (Related by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 6/315. Al-Muttaqi in Kanz al-Ummal (11/498-499) attributed it to al-Khatib and Ibn 'Asakir from Shaddad ibn Aws, and said: "In it is Isma'il ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Bindar ibn al-Muthanna al-Istarabadhi al-Wa'iz, Abu Sa'id. Al-Khatib said: he was not trusted in narration, and the hadith is munkar. Al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan (1/329): this hadith is false and has no basis. Ibn 'Asakir said: al-Wahidi related it from Ibn al-Fath Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Bindar as his son Isma'il related it from him, so he is cleared of its responsibility, and al-Khatib mentioned it only because he criticised Isma'il in it." Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Ilal al-Mutanahiyah (1/49), and al-Albani in al-Da'ifah (2/425) said: "very weak.")

When the two had concluded this contract between them, Shu'ayb commanded his daughter to give Moses a staff with which he would drive off wild beasts from his sheep. The scholars differed concerning that staff. 'Ikrimah said: Adam brought it out of Paradise, and after Adam's death Gabriel took it, and it remained with him until he met Moses by night and gave it to him. (Related by al-Tabari from 'Ikrimah: 20/67.) Others said: it was of the myrtle of Paradise. Adam carried it out of Paradise, and the prophets inherited it, and none could take it but a prophet, whom it would consume. It passed from Adam to Noah, then to Abraham, until it reached Shu'ayb, and it was the staff of the prophets with him, and he gave it to Moses. Al-Suddi said: that staff had been entrusted to him by an angel in the form of a man. He commanded his daughter to fetch a staff, so she entered and took the staff and brought it to him. When Shu'ayb saw it he said to her: "Return this staff and bring him another." She cast it down and tried to take another, but nothing came into her hand except it, until she did this three times. So he gave it to Moses, and Moses took it with him. Then the old man regretted and said: "It was a deposit," and went after him, seeking to return the staff. Moses refused to give it up and said: "It is my staff." They agreed to make the first man who met them the judge between them. An angel in the form of a man met them and ruled that the staff be thrown down, and whoever lifted it, it would be his. Moses threw down the staff, and the old man tried to take it but could not manage it. Moses took it in his hand and lifted it, and the old man left it to him. (Related by al-Tabari from al-Suddi: 20/66-67. In none of these reports is there a statement from the Prophet (ﷺ) explaining this staff, and there is no benefit in investigating such matters.)

Then, when Moses had completed the term and Shu'ayb had handed his daughter over to him, Moses said to the woman: "Ask your father to give us some of the sheep." She asked her father, and Shu'ayb said: "For you is every offspring born this year that is not of its own markings." (Al-Haythami mentioned a hadith in this regard related by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani and said: "In its isnad is Ibn Lahi'ah, in whom there is weakness, though his hadith may be good." See Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/87-88; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/387-388, where he said: "The pivot of this hadith is Ibn Lahi'ah al-Misri, who had poor memory, and I fear that its attribution to the Prophet is an error. And God knows best.") It was also said: Shu'ayb wished to reward Moses for his good shepherding, honouring him and maintaining kinship with his daughter, so he said to him: "I have given you of the kids that my sheep bear this year every spotted and speckled one," then God revealed to Moses in a dream: "Strike the water in the trough of the sheep with your staff." He said: So Moses struck the water with his staff and then gave the sheep to drink from it, and not one of them failed to bear its young between spotted and speckled. Shu'ayb knew that this was a provision God, Mighty and Majestic, had sent to Moses and his wife, so he fulfilled his condition for him and handed the sheep over to him. (Al-Haythami mentioned in this regard a hadith related by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani and said: "In its isnad is Ibn Lahi'ah, in whom there is weakness, though his hadith may be good." See Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/87-88; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/387-388, where he said: "The pivot of this hadith is Ibn Lahi'ah al-Misri, who had poor memory, and I fear that its attribution to the Prophet is an error. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 29:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When Musa had fulfilled the term﴾ means he completed it and finished with it. ﴿And set out with his family﴾. Mujahid said: When Musa had fulfilled the term, he remained after that with his father-in-law for another ten years, so he stayed with him twenty years in total. [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir said (3/388): "I have not seen this opinion from anyone other than him, though Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir have related it from him, and Allah knows best." See also al-Tabari: 20/69; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/411.]] Then he asked his father-in-law's permission to return to Egypt, and he granted it. So he set out with his family towards the side of Egypt. ﴿He saw﴾, meaning he perceived, ﴿from the side of the Mount a fire﴾. He was in the desert on a dark night, extremely cold, and his wife was experiencing labour pains. ﴿He said to his family, "Stay here; indeed I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you news from it﴾ about the way, for he had lost his way, ﴿or a burning brand from the fire, that you may warm yourselves"﴾ meaning: a piece and a flame of fire.

It has three readings. ʿĀṣim recited "jadhwatin" with a fatha on the jim; Ḥamzah recited it with a ḍamma; and the others recited it with a kasra. Qatadah and Muqatil said: it is the stick part of which has been burnt, and its plural is "jidhan" [[See also: Lisan al-ʿArab, root (j-dh-w); al-Tabari: 20/69–70.]]. ﴿That you may warm yourselves﴾ means that you may seek warmth.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verses 30–32:

﴿So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley﴾ from the side of the valley that was on the right of Musa (Moses), ﴿in the blessed place﴾ for Musa. Allah made it blessed because Allah spoke to Musa there and sent him as a prophet. And Ata' said: it means the sanctified place. ﴿From the tree﴾ from the direction of the tree. Ibn Mas'ud said: it was a green acacia that glittered [[In al-Tabari: a green, flourishing acacia tree. The samurah is a tree of the 'idah (thorny trees), with good wood.]]. Qatadah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was a thorny shrub [[A plant of the nightshade family, with thorny branches.]]. Wahb said: it was from the 'ulayq [[A thorny, climbing plant of the rose family, with red fruit, sometimes yellow, and a hard, round seed.]]. It is also related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it was the 'unnab (jujube) [[The specification of the tree's species appears to be taken from the People of the Book. See al-Tabari: 20/71; Ibn Kathir: 3/389.]]. ﴿Saying: O Musa, indeed I am Allah, the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So when he saw it moving ﴿as if it were a jann﴾ meaning a small snake, because of how quickly it moved, ﴿he turned and fled﴾ running away from it, ﴿and did not look back﴾ did not return. Then it was called out: ﴿O Musa, come forward and do not fear. Indeed, you are among the secure.﴾

﴿Insert your hand into your pocket﴾ enter, ﴿and it will come out white without harm﴾ without leprosy. It came out with a radiance like the light of the sun. ﴿And draw your arm to your side against fear﴾ the people of Kufa and Syria read it with a damma on the ra' and sukun on the ha'; Hafs reads the ra' with a fatha; and the others read both with a fatha. All of these are dialects with the meaning of fear. The meaning of the verse is: when the matter of your hand alarms you and you see its radiance, insert it into your pocket and it will return to its original condition. ("Al-janah" [wing/arm]) is the whole hand. It is also said it is the upper arm. Ata', from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Allah commanded him to press his hand to his chest [[In manuscript "A": his upper arm.]], so that what he had suffered of fear at seeing the snake would leave him. He said: no one who is frightened after Musa, if he places his hand on his chest, will have his fear removed. Mujahid said: whoever is startled and draws his two wings to himself, the fright leaves him. It is also said that the meaning of drawing in the wing is tranquility, i.e., calm your alarm and lower your side, because it is the nature of one who is afraid that his heart is agitated and his body trembles. Similar is His saying: ﴿And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy﴾ [al-Isra': 24], meaning gentleness; and His saying: ﴿And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 215], meaning: be gentle with them and soften your attitude toward them.

Al-Farra' said: by "the wing" He meant the staff; its meaning is: draw your staff to yourself. It is also said that "al-rahb" means the sleeve, in the dialect of Himyar. Al-Asma'i said: I heard some Bedouins say: "Give me what is in your rahb," meaning in your sleeve. The meaning is: draw your hand to yourself and bring it out from the sleeve, because he had taken hold of the staff while his hand was in his sleeve.

﴿These two﴾ meaning the staff and the white hand, ﴿are two proofs﴾ two signs, ﴿from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 33–34:

﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I killed a man among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾

﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent than me in tongue﴾. He said this only because of the knot (ʿuqdah) that was in his tongue from the placing of the live coal in his mouth [[This has been mentioned in the hadith of al-Futun in Surah Ta-Ha and in this surah. It is in al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/569–579. The Hafiz Ibn Kathir also mentioned it in al-Bidayah wa'l-Nihayah: 1/300–307 and said: "Thus did the Imam al-Nasa'i relate this hadith, and Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it in their tafsirs from the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun. What is most likely, and Allah knows best, is that it is mawquf (halted at a companion or successor), and that it being marfu' (traced to the Prophet) is open to question. Most of it is derived from the Isra'iliyyat, and there is in it a small amount that explicitly traces it to the Prophet in the course of the speech, and in some of what it contains there is objection and strangeness. The others read it with a jazm, as an answer to the supplication, and the confirmation is for Harun, according to the consensus. Muqatil said: "So that Pharaoh may believe me." ﴿Indeed I fear that they will deny me﴾, meaning Pharaoh and his people.

﴿He said: "We will strengthen your arm with your brother."﴾ That is: We will support you with your brother. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 28, verses 39–42:**

﴿And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land without right, and they thought that they would not be returned to Us.﴾ Nafi', Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub recited "يَرْجِعُونَ" (yarji'un) with a fatha on the yā' and a kasra on the jīm, [and the rest recited it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatha on the jīm]. [[The text between the brackets is omitted in "A".]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 43–45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book after We had destroyed the former generations﴾, meaning: the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud and others who were before Moses. ﴿As insight for mankind﴾, that is, so that they may see by means of that Book and be guided by it. ﴿And guidance﴾ from misguidance for whoever acts upon it, ﴿and mercy﴾ for whoever believes in it, ﴿that they may be mindful﴾ through what it contains of admonitions and insights.

﴿And you were not﴾, O Muhammad [[Omitted from "A".]], ﴿on the western side﴾, meaning: on the western side of the mountain. This was said by Qatadah and al-Suddi. Al-Kalbi said: on the western side of the valley. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: he means the place where Moses communed with his Lord. ﴿When We decreed to Moses the command﴾, meaning: We charged him and firmly settled the matter with him regarding the mission to Pharaoh and his people. ﴿And you were not among the witnesses﴾, present at that station, so that you could relate it from your own knowledge.

﴿But We produced generations﴾, We created nations after Moses, peace be upon him. ﴿So life grew long for them﴾, meaning: the respite was prolonged for them, so they forgot the covenant of Allah and abandoned His command. That is because Allah, exalted is He, had made many covenants with Moses and his people concerning Muhammad (ﷺ) and belief in him. When life grew long for them and generations succeeded generations, they forgot those covenants and abandoned fulfilling them.

﴿And you were not dwelling﴾, residing, ﴿among the people of Madyan﴾, as Moses and Shuʿayb had dwelt among them, ﴿reciting to them Our verses﴾, reminding them of the promise and the threat. Muqatil said: He says, you did not witness the people of Madyan so that you could recount their news to the people of Makkah. ﴿But We were sending messengers﴾, meaning: We sent you as a messenger and revealed to you a Book containing these reports, so that you recite them to them. Had it not been for that, you would not have known them and would not have informed them of them.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 28, verses 48–50:**

﴿So when the truth came to them from Us﴾: meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿They said﴾: meaning the disbelievers of Makkah. ﴿Why was he not given﴾: why was it not granted, i.e. ﴿why was Muhammad not given﴾ ﴿the like of what was given to Musa﴾ [among the signs, such as the white hand and the staff. It is also said: "the like of what was given to Musa"] [[The text between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".]] ﴿a Book all at once﴾. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verses 58–61:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy, which had been wanton in its livelihood﴾ [i.e., the people of a town] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]], ﴿so those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little﴾. That is, they grew insolent and transgressed in their livelihood. ʿAṭāʾ said: They lived in insolence, eating the provision of God and worshipping idols. ﴿So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbās, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: None dwelt in them except travellers and passers-by, for a day or an hour. Its meaning: they were not inhabited after them except with little habitation. It was also said: its meaning is that only the least of it was populated, and most of it lay in ruin. ﴿And We are the inheritors﴾ [cf. "Indeed We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it" (Maryam 19:40)].

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns until He had sent to their mother [town] a messenger﴾, that is, the towns whose people disbelieved; ﴿a messenger reciting to them Our verses﴾. He means: a messenger in its greatest and most important [town], warning them. He singled out the greatest [town] for the sending of a messenger in it, because messengers are sent to the notables, and the notables dwell in the cities, the places that are the "mother" of what surrounds them. ﴿Reciting to them Our verses﴾: Muqatil said: the messenger informs them that the punishment is descending upon them if they do not believe. ﴿And We would never destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers﴾, i.e., polytheists; He means: We destroyed them for their wrongdoing.

﴿And whatever you have been given of a thing, it is but the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment﴾, which you enjoy during the days of your life; then it is toward passing away and ending. ﴿And what is with God is better and more lasting; will you not reason?﴾ That is, that what endures is better than what perishes. The majority of reciters read "taʿqilūn" with the "tā'" (you), while Abū ʿAmr had the choice between "tā'" and "yā'" (they).

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verses 62–65:**

﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ in the world, that they were My partners.

﴿Those against whom the Word has been justified will say﴾: the punishment became due for them, and they are the leaders of misguidance. ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones whom we led astray"﴾: i.e., we invited them to error (*ghayy*), and they are the followers. ﴿We led them astray just as we went astray﴾: we misguided them as we ourselves were misguided. ﴿We disassociate ourselves before You﴾ from them. ﴿They never used to worship us﴾: some of them disowned others and became enemies, as God the Exalted said: ﴿On that Day, close friends will be enemies to one another﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67].

﴿And it will be said﴾ to the disbelievers: ﴿"Call upon your partners"﴾, i.e., the idols, so that they may save you from the punishment. ﴿But they will call upon them, and they will not respond to them﴾, i.e., they will not answer them. ﴿And they will see the punishment; if only they had been guided﴾. The answer to "law" (if only) is omitted, with the implied meaning: if only they had been guided in the world, they would not have seen the punishment.

﴿And on the Day He calls to them﴾, i.e., God asks the disbelievers, ﴿and He will say, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was among the people of Musa﴾. He was his paternal cousin, because Qarun is the son of Yashhar, the son of Qahith, the son of Lawi, the son of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), while Musa is the son of Imran, the son of Qahith. Ibn Ishaq said: Qarun was the paternal uncle of Musa. He was the brother of Imran, and they were both sons of Yashhar. Among the Children of Israel there was no one who recited the Torah better than Qarun, but he became a hypocrite, just as al-Samiri did. ﴿So he oppressed them﴾. It was said: he was an agent of Pharaoh over the Children of Israel, and he would oppress them and wrong them. Qatadah said: he oppressed them through his abundance of wealth. al-Dahhak said: he oppressed them through polytheism. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: he lengthened the hems of his garments by a span. We have also been related from Ibn Umar that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection at one who drags his garment out of arrogance." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Clothing, chapter on whoever drags his waist-wrap (10/254), and by Muslim in the Book of Clothing, chapter on the prohibition of dragging the garment, no. 2085 (3/1652); and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (12/9).] It was also said: he oppressed them through pride and haughtiness.

﴿And We gave him of treasures so much that their keys would weigh down a band of strong men﴾. The word "mafatih" is the plural of "miftah," which is that with which a door is opened. This is the view of Qatadah, Mujahid and a group of scholars. It was also said: "mafatih" means its treasuries, as in His saying: "And with Him are the keys (mafatih) of the unseen" [al-An'am: 59], meaning its treasuries. ﴿Would weigh down a band of strong men﴾, meaning they would burden them and cause them to lean over when they carried them because of their heaviness. Abu Ubaydah said: this is an instance of al-maqlub (inversion, a transposition of word order in the sentence), and its underlying sense is: "Indeed, the band would be weighed down by them." It is said: "naa fulan bi-kadha" when a person rises carrying it with difficulty.

They differed concerning the number of the "usbah" (band). Mujahid said: between ten and fifteen. al-Dahhak related from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): between three and ten. Qatadah said: between ten and forty. It was also said: forty men. It was also said: seventy. It is related from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that he said: his keys were carried by forty men at the strongest of men. Jarir related from Mansur from Khaythamah, who said: I found in the Gospel that the keys to the treasuries of Qarun were the load of sixty mules, and no single key exceeded a finger in size, and each key was a treasure.

It is said that Qarun, wherever he went, would carry the keys to his treasures with him, and they were made of iron. When they became heavy upon him, he made them of wood, and when they became heavy again, he made them of cowhide, of the length of fingers, and they would be carried with him on forty mules when he rode. [The various reports mentioned above are found in al-Tabari (20/105-110) and al-Durr al-Manthur (6/437-438). They are many and conflicting reports, none of which is traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah knows best which of them is correct.]

﴿When his people said to him﴾. His people from the Children of Israel said to Qarun: ﴿Do not exult﴾, meaning do not be insolent, do not be boastful, and do not be exultant. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the exultant﴾, meaning the insolent, the wanton, who do not thank Allah for what He has given them.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 77:**

﴿But seek, through what Allah has given you, the Abode of the Hereafter﴾. Seek, through the wealth, blessings and Paradise that Allah has given you, the means of attaining the Hereafter. This means that you stand in thankfulness to Allah for the favours He has bestowed upon you, and spend them in pursuit of the pleasure of Allah, exalted is He. ﴿And do not forget your share of this world﴾. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: do not abandon working in this world for the sake of the Hereafter, so that you may be saved from the punishment. For the true share of a person in this world is that he works for the Hereafter. Al-Suddi said: it is by giving charity and maintaining ties of kinship. Ali said: do not forget your health, your strength, your youth and your wealth, that you should seek the Hereafter through them. Abd al-Wahid al-Maliihi informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us: Abu Yazid Hatim ibn Mahbub al-Shami informed us: Husayn al-Marwazi informed us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Ja'far ibn Burqan informed us, from Ziyad ibn al-Jarrah, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man while admonishing him: "Take advantage of five before five: your youth before your old age, your health before your sickness, your wealth before your poverty, your leisure before your preoccupation, and your life before your death." The hadith is mursal [[Narrated as a mursal (a report in which the Successor omits the Companion from the chain) by: Abu Nu'aym in Hilyat al-Awliya: 4/148, and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in Iqtida al-'Ilm al-'Amal p. 218, edited by al-Albani; Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 13/223, and al-Hakim connected it in al-Mustadrak from Ibn Abbas and declared it sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed: 4/306. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/224, and Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd p. 2 with a sound chain from the mursal of Amr ibn Maymun. See: Fath al-Bari: 11/235.]]. Al-Hasan said: He was commanded to give precedence to surplus and to keep back what suffices him. Mansur ibn Zadhan said, regarding His words "and do not forget your share of this world", that it means: your sustenance and the sustenance of your family.

﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ [i.e., do good by obeying Allah] [[What is between the brackets is absent from "A".]] as Allah has done good to you with His blessings.

It was also said: be good to others as Allah has been good to you. ﴿And do not seek corruption in the land﴾: whoever disobeys Allah has sought corruption in the land. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters﴾.

[Qarun] meaning Qarun, [[said]]: ﴿He said, "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess."﴾ That is, on account of a virtue and goodness that Allah knew in me, so He found me worthy of it, and so He favored me with this wealth over you, just as He favored me with other things. It was said: it is the knowledge of alchemy (al-kīmiyā', the art of transmuting substances). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: Musa used to know alchemy, so he taught Yusha' ibn Nun a third of that knowledge, taught Kalib ibn Yuqanna a third of it, and taught Qarun a third of it. Qarun deceived the two of them until he added their knowledge to his own, and that was the cause of his wealth. [[This opinion is weak, because alchemy in itself is false knowledge, since no one can transmute substances except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For a detailed explanation, see Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/400.]] It was also said: "on account of knowledge I possess" refers to skill in trade, agriculture, and various kinds of earning. Qatada said: they will enter the Fire without reckoning and without being questioned. Mujahid said: it means the angels will not ask about them, because they recognize them by their marks. Al-Hasan said: they will not be asked a question seeking information; they will only be asked a question of reproach and rebuke.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verses 80–81:**

﴿Those who had been given knowledge said﴾. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: this refers to the rabbis (al-ahbar) of the Children of Israel. Muqatil said: "Those who had been given knowledge of what Allah promised in the Hereafter said to those who wished for the like of what Qarun had been given in this world: ﴿Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better﴾, meaning that what is with Allah of reward and recompense is better ﴿for one who believes﴾ and affirms the Oneness of Allah, ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾ rather than what Qarun was given in this world. ﴿But none will receive it except the patient﴾." Muqatil said: "It will not be granted (la yu'ta), meaning the righteous deeds." Al-Kalbi said: "It will not be given in the Hereafter." It has also been said: "This statement, which is His saying, 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better,' will not be granted except to those who are patient in obedience to Allah and patient against the adornment of this world."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. The scholars of reports (ahl al-'ilm bil-akhbar) said: Qarun was the most learned of the Children of Israel after Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both), the best reciter of the Torah, the most handsome and the wealthiest, and he had a beautiful voice. He transgressed and rebelled. The beginning of his tyranny and disobedience was that Allah revealed to Musa that he should command his people to attach to their cloaks four threads, with a blue thread at each corner, the color of the sky, so that they would remember when they looked at it, and know that I send down My speech from it. Musa said: "O Lord, would You not command them to make all their cloaks green? For the Children of Israel despise these threads." His Lord said to him: "O Musa, the small matter of My command is not small. If they do not obey Me in a small matter, they will not obey Me in a great matter." [So Musa, peace be upon him, called them] [[What is between the brackets is absent from manuscript "A".]] and said: "Indeed Allah commands you to attach to your cloaks threads of green, like the color of the sky, so that you may remember your Lord when you see them." The Children of Israel did what Musa commanded them. But Qarun became arrogant and did not obey him, and said: "Only the lords do this with their servants, in order to distinguish themselves from others." Thus this was the beginning of his disobedience and rebellion.

When Musa led the Children of Israel across the sea, the hubburah (the headship of the altar, i.e., the priesthood of sacrifice) was given to Harun. The Children of Israel used to bring their offerings to Harun, who would place them on the altar, and fire would descend from the sky and consume them. Qarun found this in himself to be a grievance, and he came to Musa and said: "O Musa, you have the prophethood and Harun has the hubburah, and I have nothing of that, though I read the Torah. I have no patience for this." Musa said to him: "I did not give it to Harun; rather, Allah gave it to him." Qarun said: "By Allah, I will not believe you until you show me its evidence." So Musa gathered the leaders of the Children of Israel and said: "Bring your staffs." He bound them together and placed them in his tent in which he worshipped Allah. They kept guard over their staffs until morning. In the morning, Harun's staff had put forth green leaves, and it was of almond wood. Musa said: "O Qarun, do you see this?" Qarun said: "By Allah, this is not more wondrous than the magic you perform." Qarun withdrew from Musa with his followers. Musa kept dealing gently with him because of the kinship between them, while he kept harming him at every time and increased only in insolence, arrogance, and enmity toward Musa. Until he built a house and made its door of gold, and overlaid its walls with sheets of gold. The chiefs of the Children of Israel used to come to him morning and evening; he fed them food, conversed with them, and made them laugh.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: When zakat was revealed to Musa, Qarun came to him and reached an arrangement with him that from every thousand dinars he would give one dinar, from every thousand dirhams one dirham, from every thousand sheep one sheep, and from every thousand of anything one of it. Then he returned to his house and calculated it, and found it to be a great amount, and his soul would not allow him to give it. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said to them: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you have obeyed him, and now he wants to take your wealth." They said: "You are our chief, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring such-and-such a prostitute (al-baghiy), and we will give her a reward so that she accuses Musa with herself. When she does so, the Children of Israel will rise against him and abandon him." They summoned her, and Qarun gave her a thousand dirhams. It was also said a thousand dinars, and it was also said a basin of gold. It was also said that he told her: "I will enrich you and make you one of my wives, on condition that you accuse Musa of adultery with yourself tomorrow when the Children of Israel are present." When the next day came, Qarun gathered the Children of Israel, then came to Musa and said: "The Children of Israel are waiting for your coming out, so that you may command them and forbid them." Musa went out to them while they were in an open place of land. He stood and said: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we will cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we will flog him eighty lashes; whoever commits fornication while he has no wife, we will flog him one hundred lashes; and whoever commits fornication while he has a wife, we will stone him until he dies." Qarun said to him: "Even if you are the one?" He said: "Even if I am the one." Qarun said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with such-and-such a woman." Musa said: "Call her. If she says so, then it is as she says." When she came, Musa said to her: "O such-and-such, did I do to you what these people say?" He was severe with her and adjured her by Him who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah, that she must tell the truth. Allah the Exalted granted her success, and she said to herself: "Today I will make a repentance better than harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "No, they lied; rather, Qarun gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you with myself." Musa fell down in prostration, weeping, and said: "O Allah, if I am Your Messenger, then be angry on my behalf." Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "I have commanded the earth to obey you, so command it as you wish." Musa said: "O Children of Israel, Allah has sent me to Qarun just as He sent me to Fir'awn. Whoever is with him, let him remain in his place, and whoever is with me, let him withdraw." They withdrew, and there remained with Qarun only two men. Then Musa said: "O earth, seize them," and the earth seized them by their feet.

In another report: Qarun was on his couch and his bedding, and the earth took him until it covered his couch. Then he said: "O earth, seize them," and it seized them up to their knees. Then he said: "O earth, seize them," and it seized them up to their waists. Then he said: "O earth [[Absent from manuscript "A".]] seize them," and it seized them up to their necks. Throughout all of this, Qarun and his companions kept humbling themselves before Musa, and Qarun kept adjuring him by Allah and by kinship, until it is reported that he adjured him seventy times, while Musa, peace be upon him, in all of that did not turn to him because of his intense anger. Then he said: "O earth, seize them," and the earth closed over them. Allah revealed to Musa: "How hard your heart is! He sought your help seventy times and you did not help him. By My might and My majesty, if he had sought My help even once, I would have helped him." And in some reports: "I will not make the earth after you obedient to anyone." [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir (3/402) and in al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (1/309–311) the destruction of Qarun because of the supplication of Musa and the disagreement of the scholars about the cause of that. Then he said: "Many commentators have mentioned here many strange Israelite narrations, which we have set aside and deliberately omitted." This indicates the source of the reports cited by al-Baghawi, may Allah have mercy on him.]]

Qatadah said: He was swallowed by the earth, and he continues to sink into the earth every day, a man's height, and will not reach its bottom until the Day of Resurrection. He said: The Children of Israel woke up whispering among themselves that Musa had only prayed against Qarun so that he could take his house, his treasures, and his wealth. Then Allah the Exalted answered Musa's prayer, and the earth swallowed up his house, his treasures, and his wealth. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. ﴿Then he had no company to help him﴾, meaning a group, ﴿against Allah﴾, meaning to protect him from Allah, ﴿nor was he among those who could defend himself﴾, meaning those who could protect themselves from what befell him of being swallowed by the earth.

Muqatil said: "It will not be granted (la yu'ta), meaning the righteous deeds." Al-Kalbi said: "It will not be given in the Hereafter." It has also been said: "This statement, which is His saying, 'Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better,' will not be granted except to those who are patient in obedience to Allah and patient against the adornment of this world."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. The scholars of reports (ahl al-'ilm bil-akhbar) said: Qarun was the most learned of the Children of Israel after Musa and Harun (peace be upon them both), the best reciter of the Torah, the most handsome and the wealthiest, and he had a beautiful voice. He transgressed and rebelled. The beginning of his tyranny and disobedience was that Allah revealed to Musa that he should command his people to attach to their cloaks four threads, with a blue thread at each corner, the color of the sky, so that they would remember when they looked at it, and know that I send down My speech from it. Musa said: "O Lord, would You not command them to make all their cloaks green? For the Children of Israel despise these threads." His Lord said to him: "O Musa, the small matter of My command is not small. If they do not obey Me in a small matter, they will not obey Me in a great matter." [So Musa, peace be upon him, called them] [[What is between the brackets is absent from manuscript "A".]] and said: "Indeed Allah commands you to attach to your cloaks threads of green, like the color of the sky, so that you may remember your Lord when you see them." The Children of Israel did what Musa commanded them. But Qarun became arrogant and did not obey him, and said: "Only the lords do this with their servants, in order to distinguish themselves from others." Thus this was the beginning of his disobedience and rebellion.

When Musa led the Children of Israel across the sea, the hubburah (the headship of the altar, i.e., the priesthood of sacrifice) was given to Harun. The Children of Israel used to bring their offerings to Harun, who would place them on the altar, and fire would descend from the sky and consume them. Qarun found this in himself to be a grievance, and he came to Musa and said: "O Musa, you have the prophethood and Harun has the hubburah, and I have nothing of that, though I read the Torah. I have no patience for this." Musa said to him: "I did not give it to Harun; rather, Allah gave it to him." Qarun said: "By Allah, I will not believe you until you show me its evidence." So Musa gathered the leaders of the Children of Israel and said: "Bring your staffs." He bound them together and placed them in his tent in which he worshipped Allah. They kept guard over their staffs until morning. In the morning, Harun's staff had put forth green leaves, and it was of almond wood. Musa said: "O Qarun, do you see this?" Qarun said: "By Allah, this is not more wondrous than the magic you perform." Qarun withdrew from Musa with his followers. Musa kept dealing gently with him because of the kinship between them, while he kept harming him at every time and increased only in insolence, arrogance, and enmity toward Musa. Until he built a house and made its door of gold, and overlaid its walls with sheets of gold. The chiefs of the Children of Israel used to come to him morning and evening; he fed them food, conversed with them, and made them laugh.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: When zakat was revealed to Musa, Qarun came to him and reached an arrangement with him that from every thousand dinars he would give one dinar, from every thousand dirhams one dirham, from every thousand sheep one sheep, and from every thousand of anything one of it. Then he returned to his house and calculated it, and found it to be a great amount, and his soul would not allow him to give it. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said to them: "O Children of Israel, Musa has commanded you in everything and you have obeyed him, and now he wants to take your wealth." They said: "You are our chief, so command us as you wish." He said: "I command you to bring such-and-such a prostitute (al-baghiy), and we will give her a reward so that she accuses Musa with herself. When she does so, the Children of Israel will rise against him and abandon him." They summoned her, and Qarun gave her a thousand dirhams. It was also said a thousand dinars, and it was also said a basin of gold. It was also said that he told her: "I will enrich you and make you one of my wives, on condition that you accuse Musa of adultery with yourself tomorrow when the Children of Israel are present." When the next day came, Qarun gathered the Children of Israel, then came to Musa and said: "The Children of Israel are waiting for your coming out, so that you may command them and forbid them." Musa went out to them while they were in an open place of land. He stood and said: "O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we will cut off his hand; whoever slanders, we will flog him eighty lashes; whoever commits fornication while he has no wife, we will flog him one hundred lashes; and whoever commits fornication while he has a wife, we will stone him until he dies." Qarun said to him: "Even if you are the one?" He said: "Even if I am the one." Qarun said: "The Children of Israel claim that you committed fornication with such-and-such a woman." Musa said: "Call her. If she says so, then it is as she says." When she came, Musa said to her: "O such-and-such, did I do to you what these people say?" He was severe with her and adjured her by Him who split the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah, that she must tell the truth. Allah the Exalted granted her success, and she said to herself: "Today I will make a repentance better than harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." She said: "No, they lied; rather, Qarun gave me a reward on condition that I accuse you with myself." Musa fell down in prostration, weeping, and said: "O Allah, if I am Your Messenger, then be angry on my behalf." Allah the Exalted revealed to him: "I have commanded the earth to obey you, so command it as you wish." Musa said: "O Children of Israel, Allah has sent me to Qarun just as He sent me to Fir'awn. Whoever is with him, let him remain in his place, and whoever is with me, let him withdraw." They withdrew, and there remained with Qarun only two men. Then Musa said: "O earth, seize them," and the earth seized them by their feet.

In another report: Qarun was on his couch and his bedding, and the earth took him until it covered his couch. Then he said: "O earth, seize them," and it seized them up to their knees. Then he said: "O earth, seize them," and it seized them up to their waists. Then he said: "O earth [[Absent from manuscript "A".]] seize them," and it seized them up to their necks. Throughout all of this, Qarun and his companions kept humbling themselves before Musa, and Qarun kept adjuring him by Allah and by kinship, until it is reported that he adjured him seventy times, while Musa, peace be upon him, in all of that did not turn to him because of his intense anger. Then he said: "O earth, seize them," and the earth closed over them. Allah revealed to Musa: "How hard your heart is! He sought your help seventy times and you did not help him. By My might and My majesty, if he had sought My help even once, I would have helped him." And in some reports: "I will not make the earth after you obedient to anyone." [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir (3/402) and in al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya (1/309–311) the destruction of Qarun because of the supplication of Musa and the disagreement of the scholars about the cause of that. Then he said: "Many commentators have mentioned here many strange Israelite narrations, which we have set aside and deliberately omitted." This indicates the source of the reports cited by al-Baghawi, may Allah have mercy on him.]]

Qatadah said: He was swallowed by the earth, and he continues to sink into the earth every day, a man's height, and will not reach its bottom until the Day of Resurrection. He said: The Children of Israel woke up whispering among themselves that Musa had only prayed against Qarun so that he could take his house, his treasures, and his wealth. Then Allah the Exalted answered Musa's prayer, and the earth swallowed up his house, his treasures, and his wealth. That is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾. ﴿Then he had no company to help him﴾, meaning a group, ﴿against Allah﴾, meaning to protect him from Allah, ﴿nor was he among those who could defend himself﴾, meaning those who could protect themselves from what befell him of being swallowed by the earth.

﴿And those who had wished to be in his place only yesterday began to say, by the morning﴾ ... Those who had wished for what God had given him of wealth and adornment became regretful for that wish. The Arabs use *asbaha* (became), *adha* (became in the afternoon) and *amsa* (became in the evening) to express a change of state. They say: "So-and-so became (*asbaha*) a scholar (*'aliman*)" [[In manuscript "B": *ghaniman*, "wealthy".]], "became (*adha*) destitute (*mu'diman*)," and "became (*amsa*) sad (*hazinan*)."

﴿They say, "Wow! God..."﴾ Scholars differ over the meaning of this expression. Mujahid said it means "Do you not know?" and Qatadah said it means "Do you not see?" Al-Farra' said: it is an expression of affirmation, like a man saying, "Do you not see God's handiwork and His kindness?" He mentioned that someone who heard a Bedouin woman say to her husband, "Where is your son?" was told that he replied, "Wa-ka-annahu (wayka'anna) is behind the house," meaning, "Do you not see him behind the house?"

It is reported from al-Hasan that it is a word of introduction, its implied meaning being: "Indeed God extends provision." It was also said that it is an alerting particle, equivalent to *ala* (surely). Qutrub said: *wayka* means *waylaka* (woe to you), with the lam omitted, as Antarah said:

"And indeed she was healed, and her sickness was cured,
by the saying of the horsemen, 'Woe to you, Antar, advance!'"

[[The verse is by Antarah, cited by al-Farra' and al-Tabari as evidence.]] That is, *waylaka*. *Anna* is in the accusative, governed by an implied *i'lam anna Allaha* ("know that God..."). Al-Khalil said: *wayy* is separated from *ka-anna*, and its meaning is wonder, as you say, "Wai, why did you do that!" The people expressed regret, saying "Wai!" while regretting what had passed from them. *Ka-anna* means "I think and estimate that," as you say, "Ka-anna relief has come to you," meaning "I think and estimate that."

﴿God extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it﴾, that is, He widens and narrows it.

﴿Had not God been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up﴾. Hafs and Ya'qub read *lakhasafa* with a fatha on the *kha'* and the *sin*, while the majority read it with a damma on the *kha'* and a kasra on the *sin*.

﴿Wow! Indeed the disbelievers do not prosper.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verses 83–85:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness (ʿuluww) in the earth﴾. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: [this means] arrogance (istikbar) towards faith. ʿAtaʾ said: "ʿuluww" is [haughtiness and] domineering over people and treating them with contempt. Al-Hasan said: [it means] you did not seek nobility and honour with a ruler. It is related from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that it was revealed concerning the people of humility among the lowly and the people of power. [[Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn ʿAsakir from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him; see al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/444.]] ﴿Nor corruption (fasad)﴾. Al-Kalbi said: it is calling to the worship of other than Allah. ʿIkrimah said: taking people's wealth unjustly. Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil said: acting in disobedience.

﴿And the good end is for the God-fearing (al-muttaqun)﴾, i.e., the praiseworthy outcome is for those who fear the punishment of Allah by performing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. Qatadah said: Paradise is for the God-fearing.

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it, and they will be safe from terror that Day﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you﴾, i.e., He revealed the Qur'an to you, according to the view of most exegetes. ʿAtaʾ said: He made it obligatory upon you to act by the Qur'an. ﴿Will surely bring you back to a place of return (maʿad)﴾, to Makkah. This is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: 8/509–510.]] It is also the saying of Mujahid. Al-Qutaybi said: the maʿad of a man is his homeland, because he departs and then returns to his homeland. [[The words "to his homeland" are omitted in manuscript "b". The wording of Ibn Qutaybi in al-Mushkil, p. 425, is: "...for he travels through the lands, roams the earth, and then returns to his homeland...", which is clearer and more accurate than what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted.]] That is because when the Prophet ﷺ left the cave emigrating to Madinah, he travelled by a route other than the main road, fearing pursuit. When he was safe and returned to the road, he descended at al-Juhfah between Makkah and Madinah, and when he recognised the road to Makkah he longed for it. Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "Do you long for your land and your birthplace?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an for you will surely bring you back to a place of return﴾." [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.]] This verse was revealed at al-Juhfah; it is neither Makkan nor Madani. [[Ibn Kathir said (3/404): "This statement of al-Dahhak implies that this verse is Madani, although the whole surah is Makkan, and Allah knows best."]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding "will surely bring you back to a place of return": [it means] to death. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 20/125, and Ibn Abi Hatim. The hafiz said in al-Fath (8/510): its chain is not objectionable.]] Al-Zuhri and ʿIkrimah said: [it means] to the Day of Resurrection. [[Ibn Abi Hatim narrated through Mujahid: "He will revive you on the Day of Resurrection." As for al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, they said: it is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Ya'la narrated through Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn ʿAli who said: I asked Abu Sa'id about this verse, and he said: its maʿad is its afterlife. Its chain contains Jabir al-Ju'fi, who is weak. See Fath al-Bari: 8/510.]] It was also said: [it means] to Paradise. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 20/124; its chain is weak, as in the same place in al-Fath.]]

﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance﴾ [i.e., your Lord knows who has come with guidance], and this is an answer to the disbelievers of Makkah when they said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed you are in clear error." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: Say to them: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance, meaning himself, ﴿and who is in manifest error﴾, meaning the polytheists. Its meaning is: He knows best about both groups.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 28, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you did not expect that the Book would be bestowed upon you﴾, meaning: the Qur'an would be revealed to you, ﴿except as a mercy from your Lord﴾. Al-Farra' said: this is an exception of the disconnected type (al-istithna' al-munqati', an exception where what follows is not of the same category as what precedes), its meaning being: "But your Lord has shown you mercy and so gave you the Qur'an." ﴿So never be a supporter (zahir) for the disbelievers﴾, meaning: a helper to them in their religion. Muqatil said: this was when he was called to the religion of his forefathers, so Allah reminded him of His blessings and forbade him from supporting them in what they were upon.

﴿And let them not turn you away from the signs of Allah﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿after they have been sent down to you. And call to your Lord﴾, to knowing Him and affirming His oneness, ﴿and do not be among the polytheists﴾. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The address is outwardly to the Prophet (ﷺ), but what is meant is the people of his religion, that is: do not support the disbelievers or agree with them.

﴿And do not call upon another god besides Allah. There is no god but Him. Everything will perish except His Face﴾, that is, except Him. It is also said: except His dominion. Abu al-'Aliyah said: except what is intended for His Face. ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾, that is, the final decision, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, you will be brought back in the Hereafter, and He will recompense you for your deeds.
